title: Private Britain & Scotland Tour.

private.name: Private Vehicle
private.blurb: London, the Peak District, Edinburgh, the Highlands and Loch Ness on a private coach, with a self-guided day in Edinburgh and an optional trip to the Isle of Skye.

transport.3: Private vehicle for 8 hours to Stonehenge and Bath, with included entrance tickets.

days.title: Arrival in London
days.desc: Welcome to London. Transfer to your hotel and spend the rest of the day exploring at your own pace — Oxford Street and Harrods are must-visits for shopping. Overnight in London.

days.title: London
days.desc: A 3-hour guided city tour takes in London's iconic landmarks, followed by standard London Eye tickets and a Thames river cruise. Overnight in London.
days.shopping: Oxford Street and the surrounding grid of Regent Street and Bond Street cover everything from flagship department stores to luxury boutiques.

days.title: London — Stonehenge & Bath
days.desc: A day trip to the ancient mysteries of Stonehenge and the Georgian elegance of Bath, with included entrance tickets tracing both sites' history. Return to London for another night. Overnight in London.
days.experience: Bath's Roman Baths, built around natural hot springs, have drawn visitors for close to 2,000 years — the same waters still flow through the original Roman-era chambers.

days.title: London to Manchester
days.desc: Travel from London to Manchester with a stop in the Peak District to take in its scenic countryside. Overnight in Manchester.

days.title: Manchester to Edinburgh
days.desc: Journey north from Manchester to Edinburgh, pausing in the Lake District's picturesque landscapes. Edinburgh awaits with its medieval Old Town and elegant Georgian New Town. Overnight in Edinburgh.

days.title: Edinburgh
days.desc: A self-guided day to explore Edinburgh at your own pace — Edinburgh Castle, Princes Street, and the historic Royal Mile. Overnight in Edinburgh.
days.taste: Haggis, neeps and tatties at one of the pubs along the Royal Mile, ideally with a dram of single malt to finish.

days.title: Edinburgh to Inverness
days.desc: Travel from Edinburgh to Inverness, passing legendary Loch Ness and the Scottish Highlands. Inverness, the Highland capital, sits on the River Ness with sites including Inverness Castle and the Caledonian Canal. Overnight in Inverness.

days.title: Inverness — Isle of Skye
days.desc: A day trip to the Isle of Skye, taking in rugged landscapes and ancient castles, including the Old Man of Storr and the Fairy Pools. Return to Inverness for the evening. Overnight in Inverness.

days.title: Inverness to Glasgow
days.desc: Travel from Inverness to Glasgow via Loch Lomond and historic Fort William. Glasgow, Scotland's largest city, is known for its arts scene and industrial heritage. Overnight in Glasgow.

days.title: Departure
days.desc: A private transfer takes you from your hotel to Glasgow Airport, concluding your journey through England and Scotland's diverse landscapes and cities.

about.title: Best season
about.body: May–September for the mildest weather and longest daylight for the Highlands drives; the Isle of Skye day trip is especially weather-dependent, so a summer visit gives the best odds of clear views.

about.title: Weather
about.body: Temperate but changeable throughout: 15–20°C in summer, rarely far below freezing in winter, but rain is possible in any season, especially in the Highlands and the Lake District.

about.title: Currency & docs
about.body: The Pound Sterling (£) is the currency across England and Scotland. The UK is not in the Schengen Area, so check current entry requirements for your passport separately from any Schengen visa.

goodToKnow.title: Long driving days
goodToKnow.body: Several days involve 4+ hours on the road between cities — the Peak District, Lake District and Highland stops break up the journey, but pack entertainment for the transfers.

goodToKnow.title: Isle of Skye weather
goodToKnow.body: Skye's landscapes are dramatic but exposed — check the forecast the night before and dress for wind and rain regardless of the season.

goodToKnow.title: What to pack
goodToKnow.body: A proper waterproof jacket for the Highlands and Skye; layers, since temperatures shift quickly between coast, glen and city.

goodToKnow.title: Tipping
goodToKnow.body: 10–12.5% is standard in restaurants across England and Scotland, often already added as a service charge for larger groups — check the bill before tipping twice.
